:::{#exm-matrix-condition-number}
#### The condition number of a matrix with nearly parallel columns

Let $\matr{A} = \sbmat{ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1.01 }$.
Its columns, $(1, 1)$ and $(1, 1.01)$, are nearly parallel.
We find its [singular values](#def-singular-values) and their [ratio](algebra-sums.qmd#def-ratio),
then repeat after multiplying every entry by $1000$:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: matrix-condition-number-r
#| code-fold: false
a_mcn <- matrix(c(1, 1, 1, 1.01), nrow = 2)
sv_mcn <- svd(a_mcn)$d
sv_mcn_scaled <- svd(1000 * a_mcn)$d
sv_mcn
sv_mcn[1] / sv_mcn[2]
sv_mcn_scaled[1] / sv_mcn_scaled[2]
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: matrix-condition-number-python
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np

a_mcn = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.01]])
sv_mcn = np.linalg.svd(a_mcn, compute_uv=False)
sv_mcn_scaled = np.linalg.svd(1000 * a_mcn, compute_uv=False)
print(sv_mcn)
print(sv_mcn[0] / sv_mcn[1])
print(sv_mcn_scaled[0] / sv_mcn_scaled[1])
```

:::

The [singular values](#def-singular-values) are `r round(sv_mcn[1], 3)` and `r round(sv_mcn[2], 4)`,
so $\condnum(\matr{A}) =$ `r round(sv_mcn[1] / sv_mcn[2], 1)`.
Multiplying every entry by $1000$ multiplies both singular values by $1000$,
so the [condition number](#def-matrix-condition-number) is still `r round(sv_mcn_scaled[1] / sv_mcn_scaled[2], 1)`.

:::
